A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing content to be matched despite substantial reorganization and a changed title.

before.justification: v2 reports mathematical proofs and analytically derived toy-network examples. Neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical experiments, simulations or data analyses.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical. Its added pseudocode, complexity examples and proofs do not report experimental execution or empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The P_r and M_k relaxations, input-copying network transformation and convex-polytope partitioning strategy are retained. Algorithm 1 documents the existing partitioning approach rather than establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical datasets or training/evaluation benchmarks. The extension to sigmoid and tanh concerns theoretical applicability, not newly evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: No empirically evaluated comparator set changes. The Triangle/k-ReLU versus M1 example is retained; v3's additional DeepPoly and IBP comparisons are mathematical complexity arguments.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, training budgets, model configurations or testing protocols. v3's partition-complexity definition is a theoretical definition rather than an experimental metric change.

E4.justification: No experimental ablations, sensitivity studies or robustness analyses are introduced. The added IBP example and Appendix H's max-network separation are formal derivations assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured performance results. The shared max-function example retains the exact upper bound 1 and Triangle/k-ReLU bound 1.5; changes to formal complexity bounds and mathematical examples are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v3 replaces v2's explicit product_j min(2^m_j, 2^d_j - 1) partition bound with activation-pattern definitions and Proposition 5.6's comparison bounds. It adds non-polynomial-activation reasoning, Corollary 5.2 on piecewise-linear expressivity, and the exponential-separation derivation in Appendix H. Appendix E.3 also replaces the higher-dimensional construction and adds the missing T scaling to the one-dimensional proof.

C1.justification: The retained ReLU incompleteness and augmented-completeness claims are broadened by a barrier claim covering non-polynomial activations. v3 also foregrounds full piecewise-linear expressivity and a general partition-complexity separation between single-neuron and multi-neuron relaxations, replacing v2's more specific P1 partition bound.

C2.justification: v2 emphasizes input partitioning over hidden-space branching; v3 emphasizes multi-neuron bounding within branch-and-bound and tailored certified training. Appendix D adds specific cautions about partitioning and merging costs, while the earlier ReLU-only limitation is replaced by the proposed activation extension.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds Algorithm 1 with partition bookkeeping and bound aggregation, making the existing strategy more explicit. v3 also clarifies optimal LP solving assumptions. Neither version supplies executable implementation details, hardware measurements or code access.

R1.justification: Related work expands to discuss PRIMA, tightened relaxations, additional MILP formulations and prior single-hidden-layer expressivity results. New Hornik and Arora citations support the added theory. The central positioning as a general theoretical study of multi-neuron relaxations remains.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the title, abstract and introduction, introduces explicit contribution bullets, and places incompleteness before completeness. Related work moves to Appendix A, the standalone max-function section becomes a case study in Section 5.1, and the discussion and appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two columns to one. Retained diagrams are resized and repositioned, the incompleteness illustration is recolored, and v3 adds the network-transformation Figure 6 and the Algorithm 1 display.

improvement.justification: v3 improves organization, documents partitioning with pseudocode and corrects the missing T scaling. However, its new general lower-bound proof in Appendix G.2 assumes every unstable neuron must be split, although the retained Triangle example gives exact bounds for an unstable ReLU without splitting. Appendix F.2 also invokes W2/W3 from the construction replaced in E.3. These exposition gains and new proof problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
